project_requirements.title: What the call wants
project_requirements.question: What must the project address, develop and achieve?

cards.title: Central object
cards.question: What is the principal thing the project must develop?
cards.answer: Demonstrate a sustainable technology for refurbishing an existing hydropower plant.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 143–144 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 143–144 · Expected Outcome

cards.title: Scope
cards.question: Which activities fall within the funding opportunity's scope?
cards.answer: Demonstrate a sustainable refurbishment of an existing hydropower plant. Options include turbines, materials, digital controls, climate models, maintenance or new operating strategies.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 143–144 · Scope

cards.title: Problem
cards.question: What type of problem or need must justify the project, and where must it originate?
cards.answer: Ageing hydropower plants need to handle new operating patterns, climate pressures and the variable generation on the power system.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 143–144 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 143–144 · Expected Outcome

cards.title: Deliverables
cards.question: Which concrete outputs must the project produce?
cards.answer: Provide a plant demonstration and a socioeconomic and environmental sustainability assessment that includes biodiversity.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 143–144 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 143–144 · Expected Outcome

cards.title: Impact
cards.question: Which wider system outcomes and impacts must the project support?
cards.answer: Improve the fleet’s contribution to a stable grid alongside variable renewables. The work should also strengthen European technical capability and adaptation to climate change.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 143–144 · Expected Outcome

cards.title: After the project
cards.question: How must the result be replicated, taken up and kept in use after the project?
cards.answer: Plan how the refurbishment results can be used and shared. Include a commercialisation strategy if developing an applicable product, process or service.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 143–144 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 3–4 · A — Admissibility

cards.title: Number of partners
cards.question: What is the permitted or required consortium size?
cards.answer: The proposal needs at least three independent funded partners in three different eligible countries. At least one must be established in a European Union Member State. The other two must be established in different Member States or countries associated with Horizon Europe (countries formally participating in the European research programme).
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 13 · Consortium composition

cards.title: Partner composition
cards.question: Which types of partners must the consortium include?
cards.answer: Include partners with access to an existing hydropower plant and skills to refurbish it and assess sustainability. Select any grid partner based on the chosen fleet-control or integration work.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 143–144 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 13 · Consortium composition

cards.title: Distribution of work
cards.question: How must work and budget be distributed among partners?

cards.title: Coordinator
cards.question: What type of organisation may or must act as lead applicant?
cards.answer: The group appoints a funded partner to lead the work on hydropower refurbishments and represent it to the funder.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 36 · Consortium roles, Coordinator and Associated partners

project_requirements.title: TenneT's position
project_requirements.question: What is TenneT's position within the consortium?

cards.title: Coordinate
cards.question: Can TenneT apply or coordinate, and under which conditions?
cards.answer: TenneT could coordinate the project if it can contribute grid-integration or flexibility evidence to an existing-plant refurbishment. The applicants choose their coordinator (the funded partner that represents the group to the funder).
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 5, 11–13 · B — Eligibility
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 36 · Consortium roles, Coordinator and Associated partners
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 143–144 · Specific conditions
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 143–144 · Scope

cards.title: Participate
cards.question: Can TenneT take part without receiving funding?
cards.answer: TenneT could contribute grid-integration or flexibility evidence to an existing-plant refurbishment as an associated partner (an organisation that works without a grant). It would cover its own costs and would not count towards the minimum number of funded partners.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 5, 11–13 · B — Eligibility
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 36 · Consortium roles, Coordinator and Associated partners

cards.title: Receive funding
cards.question: Can TenneT receive funding, and which funding rate or cost rules apply?
cards.answer: TenneT can receive up to 70% of eligible costs (project costs the grant rules allow) for qualifying work. The Dutch entity could contribute grid-integration or flexibility evidence to an existing-plant refurbishment. Budget at least 30% of those costs from other resources. The rate helps set a lump sum (a fixed grant paid for accepted work rather than reimbursing actual spending). The topic excludes organisations directly or indirectly controlled by China or by a legal entity established there.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 31–32 · Form of grant, funding rate and maximum grant amount

cards.title: TenneT's likely contribution
cards.question: What contribution would make TenneT credible and useful within the project?
cards.answer: TenneT could define flexibility needs and assess the effect of a proposed fleet control or grid-integration change. An existing plant operator would need to host the demonstration.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 143–144 · Scope

project_requirements.title: Innovation
project_requirements.question: What type of innovation must the project develop?

cards.title: Innovation threshold
cards.question: Must the project produce genuinely new knowledge or technology, or may it integrate and apply existing solutions?
cards.answer: The project can improve existing equipment or operating methods. The innovation must be demonstrated through refurbishment at an existing plant.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 143–144 · Scope

cards.title: Innovation object
cards.question: In what must the project innovate?
cards.answer: The call covers physical equipment, plant modelling, instrumentation, controls, materials and maintenance methods for changing load and climate conditions.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 143–144 · Scope

cards.title: Development stages
cards.question: Which development stages must the project cover?
cards.answer: Develop or adapt the selected technology, demonstrate it in a plant refurbishment and assess its socioeconomic and environmental sustainability.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 143–144 · Scope

cards.title: Maturity
cards.question: Which maturity level is expected at the start and end of the project?
cards.answer: The work should reach TRL 6–7 (technology readiness level: technology demonstrated in relevant or operational conditions) by project end. The call allows work to start at any maturity level.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 143–144 · Specific conditions

project_requirements.title: Work
project_requirements.question: Which activities or work structure must the project cover?

cards.title: Demonstration
cards.question: Where and under which conditions must the solution be demonstrated?
cards.answer: Apply the work to an existing hydropower plant. Use the refurbishment setting to assess the selected technical and environmental changes.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 143–144 · Scope

cards.title: Integration
cards.question: How must the activities fit together and with existing systems?
cards.answer: Fit new components or controls to an existing plant. Where the project covers fleet controls, show how the refurbished plant helps respond to changing electricity-system conditions.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 143–144 · Scope

cards.title: Evidence
cards.question: What must the demonstration prove?
cards.answer: Provide an assessment of socioeconomic and environmental sustainability, including biodiversity. Support the selected refurbishment case with demonstrated technical results.

funding_timing_submission.title: Funding
funding_timing_submission.question: How much funding can the project receive?

cards.title: Funding envelope
cards.answer:
The Commission indicates EUR 17 million for hydropower refurbishments. It expects 2 awards.
- Grant request: Around EUR 8.5 million per project. Different requests are eligible.
- Funding form: Lump sum (a fixed grant paid for accepted work rather than reimbursing actual spending).
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 143–144 · Specific conditions
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · p. 48 · Overview of this call
Demonstration of hydropower technologies for efficient and forward-looking refurbishment of existing hydropower plants · Budget overview

cards.title: Funding rate and co-financing
cards.answer:
For-profit organisations can receive up to 70% towards hydropower refurbishments. The rate is used to set the lump sum (a fixed grant paid for accepted work rather than reimbursing actual spending).
- For-profit organisations: Up to 70% of eligible costs (project costs the grant rules allow), leaving at least 30% to cover.
- Non-profit legal entities: Up to 100% of eligible costs (project costs the grant rules allow).
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 31–32 · Form of grant, funding rate and maximum grant amount

cards.title: Budget constraints
cards.answer:
Plan the budget for hydropower refurbishments using the cost categories allowed by the grant. Use estimates to set the fixed grant.
- Eligible costs (project costs the grant rules allow): Estimate costs by beneficiary (organisations formally responsible for funded work), work package (separately planned blocks of project work) and budget category.
- Subcontracting or equipment: Apply best-value and conflict-of-interest rules. Estimate equipment depreciation when applicable.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 27 · E — Documents
Lump Sum Funding in Horizon Europe: What do I need to know? · pp. 7, 27, 34–36 · Writing a lump sum proposal and detailed budget table

cards.title: Cash flow and financial exposure
cards.answer:
Plan cash flow for hydropower refurbishments around acceptance of completed blocks of work.
- Payment model: Pre-financing (an advance at the start of the grant) followed by reporting-period payments for completed work packages (separately planned blocks of project work). Incomplete packages can delay payment.
- Retention or guarantee: The mutual insurance mechanism (a common fund covering grant recovery risks) deducts 5–8% of the maximum grant from pre-financing.
- Financial reporting or audit: Retain evidence of task completion. Actual-cost reporting is not required for the lump sum (a fixed grant paid for accepted work rather than reimbursing actual spending).
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 33 · Reporting & payment arrangements
Lump Sum Funding in Horizon Europe: What do I need to know? · pp. 17–23 · Payment schedule, Reporting and payment, Keeping records

funding_timing_submission.title: Timing
funding_timing_submission.question: What timing should the proposal submission and project follow?

cards.title: Application route
cards.answer:
Apply for hydropower refurbishments through the European Funding & Tenders Portal in one stage.
- Full proposal: 1 December 2027, 17:00 Brussels time. Submit Part A (online administration form) and Part B (technical proposal) with a 45-page limit.
- Opening: 4 August 2027.

cards.title: Project window
cards.answer:
The grant agreement (the contract setting the funded work and payment rules) sets the start date and duration for hydropower refurbishments.
- Required start: Work normally starts after the grant agreement is signed. A reasoned exception needs approval.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 30–31 · Starting date & project duration

cards.title: Decision and contracting
cards.answer:
The Commission’s timetable for assessing and contracting hydropower refurbishments is indicative.
- Expected invitation or assessment result: Around five months from the full-proposal deadline.
- Grant agreement (the contract setting the funded work and payment rules): Around eight months from the full-proposal deadline.
- Conditions before starting: The beneficiaries (organisations formally responsible for funded work) must conclude a written consortium agreement (the partners’ written agreement on how the project will run).
cards.sources:

funding_timing_submission.title: Application
funding_timing_submission.question: Mandatory information to include in the application

cards.title: Mandatory submission package — pass/fail
cards.answer:
Use the portal’s forms to submit the proposal and supporting documents for hydropower refurbishments.
- Application form: Complete online Part A and upload technical Part B and applicable annexes.
- Registration: Beneficiaries (organisations formally responsible for funded work) and affiliated entities (organisations legally linked to funded partners) need a participant identification code before submission.
- Partner documents: The coordinator confirms its authority to act for the applicant group at submission. Participants sign declarations of honour (signed confirmations of eligibility and other requirements) before grant signature.
- Budget: Attach the detailed budget table from the submission system.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 27 · E — Documents
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 5 · Entities eligible to participate

cards.title: Evaluation and selection — scored or ranked
cards.answer:
Hydropower refurbishments proposals compete on research quality, impact and the quality of the delivery plan.
- Evaluation criteria: Excellence, impact, and quality and efficiency of implementation.
- Thresholds: At least 3/5 on each criterion and 10/15 overall.
- Ranking rules: Ties first favour uncovered topic aspects. The next criteria are impact then excellence.
- Weighting: The impact score (the score for what the project is expected to achieve) has a 1.5 multiplier for ranking.
- Budget assessment: Ineligible or overstated costs can reduce the lump sum (a fixed grant paid for accepted work rather than reimbursing actual spending).
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 23–26 · D — Award criteria
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 28–29 · Evaluation procedure and ranking
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 27 · E — Documents

cards.title: Conditional and exceptional requirements
cards.answer:
Prepare for the hydropower call’s ownership checks and address satellite rules where relevant.
- Conditional — Refurbishment demonstration: Provide an assessment covering socioeconomic sustainability, environmental sustainability and biodiversity.
- Conditional — Satellite data or services: Use Copernicus for Earth observation and/or Galileo or the European Geostationary Navigation Overlay Service for satellite positioning, navigation or timing where the proposal uses the covered services.
- Conditional — China control: Entities directly or indirectly controlled by China or an entity established there are ineligible.
- Exception — Transfer of results: The granting authority may object to a transfer of ownership or to exclusive licensing (giving another party sole rights to use the results) for up to four years after the project ends.
